exposure: urinary phthalate metabolites (9 individual: MEP, MBzP, DEHP metabolites; 5 summary measures: Plastic, AA, Phthalates)
cohort: Pre- and perimenopausal women from the Midlife Women's Health Study (MWHS) (n=751) participated in the study.
finding: Increased concentrations of certain urinary phthalate metabolites were longitudinally associated with lower testosterone and estradiol, and higher sub-ovulatory progesterone levels during the menopausal transition.
